selection.text: A dose-response curve plots the magnitude of a physiological or behavioral response (e.g., drug effect, immune response) against the amount (dose) of an applied stimulus. A peak at an intermediate dose arises because low doses often stimulate a beneficial or activating effect, while higher doses can lead to receptor saturation, functional inhibition, or toxic/destructive effects, causing the response to rise to a maximum and then decline. Thus the curve reflects the balance between activation and adverse effects, producing an optimal (peak) response at a dose lower than the amount required to cause maximal toxicity.
